lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Skill model: renewals, expiries, and advance reminders

objective: Learners design a three-tier reminder ladder (advance, mid, final) that they can apply to any renewal-type item, then test it on invented examples, so the skill transfers to whatever they actually need to renew later rather than being tied to one specific case.
scenario: Working with three fictional renewal-type items and invented dates (for example, a made-up membership, a made-up permit-like renewal, and a made-up subscription), the learner sets an advance reminder, a mid-point check, and a final deadline reminder for each, then explains the spacing logic they used.
safetyNotes: All renewal items and dates in this practice are invented; no real account, subscription, or document renewal date is required.
materials: the three provided fictional renewal-item prompts

tasks.directions: Before building the ladder, think about a time a deadline snuck up on you.

prompts.text: Think of any deadline (school or otherwise) that snuck up on you before. What would an earlier reminder have needed to look like to actually help?

tasks.directions: For the first fictional renewal item, set an advance, mid, and final reminder with invented dates.

prompts.text: I set an advance reminder well before the invented deadline.
I set a mid-point check-in reminder.
I set a final reminder close to the invented deadline.

tasks.directions: Apply the same three-tier ladder to the second and third fictional renewal items, then explain your spacing.

prompts.text: Show the three reminder dates for both remaining fictional items, and explain in one or two sentences why you spaced them the way you did.

tasks.directions: Reflect on which tier matters most.

prompts.text: Of the three tiers, which one do you think you would be most likely to ignore in real life, and why?

remediation: If the learner's three reminders are bunched close together instead of genuinely staggered (for example, all three within the final week), reteach by having them mark the deadline on a blank timeline first, then place the advance reminder at roughly the timeline's midpoint before adding the other two.
extension: Have the learner design a fourth tier for a renewal item with real consequences for missing it entirely (not just inconvenience), and explain what changes about the reminder ladder when the stakes are higher.
